item.title: Russian scientists to search for ice up to 1.5 million years old in Antarctica

item.content:encoded:
Russian scientists to search for ice up to 1.5 million years old in Antarctica Staff from the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute (AARI) will set out in search of ancient ice dating back around 1.5 million years. Using this ice, polar researchers will study the concentration of greenhouse gases in the ancient atmosphere. This is important for verifying modern climate models, according to the website of the Russian Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment. Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Staff from the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute (AARI) will set out in search of ancient ice dating back around 1.5 million years. Using this ice, polar researchers will study the concentration of greenhouse gases in the ancient atmosphere. This is important for verifying modern climate models, according to the website of the Russian Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment. The composition of ice deposits holds information about past air temperatures. According to AARI Director Aleksander Makarov, around 50 million years ago, the concentration of carbon dioxide (CO₂) in the Earth’s atmosphere was significantly higher than it is today. There was no ice sheet in Antarctica at that time, and sea levels were approximately 65 metres higher than they are now. The research aims to uncover crucial information about a major transition in Earth's climate history, when the periodicity of glacial cycles underwent significant changes. Scientists believe that examining ice samples from this period could help explain the factors behind these climatic shifts and improve the accuracy of climate predictions. "Our task is to find ice in Antarctica that is up to 1.5 million years old. It is at this juncture in the planet’s climate history that significant changes in the periodicity of glacial cycles are recorded. Understanding the reasons behind this transition is critically important for testing climate models. We need to understand where the boundaries of a climate suitable for life lie," Makarov said. Russia's Minister of Natural Resources and Environment Aleksander Kozlov said that findings from ancient Antarctic ice would expand the global scientific community's understanding of how Earth's climate developed over millions of years. He added that the research would also help scientists identify the natural limits of climate variability. Ice cores preserve traces of the atmosphere from the period in which they formed, allowing researchers to examine historical greenhouse gas concentrations and reconstruct past environmental conditions. Such findings can provide valuable evidence for understanding long-term climate patterns and assessing present-day climate changes. The search for ice dating back up to 1.5 million years is part of a long-term scientific programme. Russian researchers have already collected and analysed ancient ice samples estimated to be around 1.2 million years old. The upcoming expedition will seek to extend this research further into Earth's climate past. (ANI)

item.title: US goods trade deficit widens 10.7% to USD 149.5 billion in October as imports surge
item.description: The United States' goods trade deficit widened by 10.7 per cent month-on-month to USD 149.5 billion in October 2026, compared to USD 135.1 billion in September, as growth in imports outpaced that of ...
item.content:encoded:
US goods trade deficit widens 10.7% to USD 149.5 billion in October as imports surge The United States' goods trade deficit widened by 10.7 per cent month-on-month to USD 149.5 billion in October 2026, compared to USD 135.1 billion in September, as growth in imports outpaced that of exports, according to advance estimates released by the US Census Bureau on Friday. ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 19:23 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 19:23 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States' goods trade deficit widened by 10.7 per cent month-on-month to USD 149.5 billion in October 2026, compared to USD 135.1 billion in September, as growth in imports outpaced that of exports, according to advance estimates released by the US Census Bureau on Friday. On a year-on-year basis, the goods trade deficit surged by over 143 per cent from USD 61.4 billion recorded in October 2025. "The international trade deficit was $149.5 billion in October, up $14.4 billion from $135.1 billion in September," the US Census Bureau said in its Advance Economic Indicators Report. Goods imports rose by 6.1 per cent month-on-month to USD 365.3 billion in October, while exports increased by 3.2 per cent to USD 215.8 billion. "Exports of goods for October were $215.8 billion, $6.7 billion more than September exports. Imports of goods for October were $365.3 billion, $21.1 billion more than September imports," the report said. On an annual basis, US goods imports surged by 42.4 per cent, significantly outpacing the 10.6 per cent growth in exports. The sharp increase in imports was led by capital goods, which registered an 80 per cent year-on-year growth and an 8.5 per cent sequential increase to USD 171.4 billion in October. Imports of industrial supplies, including petroleum and petroleum products, increased by 33.5 per cent year-on-year, while consumer goods and automotive vehicle imports rose by 16.6 per cent and 8.4 per cent, respectively. On the exports front, capital goods recorded a 29.2 per cent year-on-year increase, while exports of industrial supplies rose by 3.6 per cent. However, exports of automotive vehicles and consumer goods declined by 5 per cent each. The widening of the goods trade deficit comes amid Washington's renewed push for tariffs on its trading partners over alleged structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors. On November 25, the United States Trade Representative (USTR) announced proposed tariff actions following 14 investigations under Section 301 of US trade law. Washington has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, with certain exemptions, while indicating that the rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if India reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade addressing the findings of the investigation. Meanwhile, US wholesale inventories increased by 0.9 per cent month-on-month and 8.5 per cent year-on-year to USD 1,023.4 billion in October. Retail inventories also rose by 0.8 per cent sequentially and 5.1 per cent annually to USD 893.2 billion during the month. The figures are adjusted for seasonal variations but not for price changes. The October trade figures are advance estimates, with complete data to be published in the upcoming US International Trade in Goods and Services report. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Ra’am party chair Mansour Abbas to address "definition of Hamas" on Saturday ahead of Eisenkot coalition push: Report The Times of Israel reported that Abbas is scheduled to make the statement in an interview with journalist Dana Weiss on Channel 12. Confirming the broadcast, Abbas said in a statement carried by Channel 12, “On Saturday night, my interview with [journalist] Dana Weiss will be broadcast on Channel 12 news. I will address the definition of Hamas.”  ANI | The Times Of Israel Reported That Abbas Is Scheduled To Make The Statement In An Interview With Journalist Dana Weiss On Channel 12 Confirming The Broadcast, Abbas Said In A Statement Carried By Channel 12, “On Saturday Night, My Interview With | Updated: 27-11-2026 14:42 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 14:42 IST

Ra’am party chairman Mansour Abbas (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Ra’am party chairman Mansour Abbas is set to publicly declare that he recognises Hamas as a terror group during a television interview on Saturday night, a potential political shift that could clear an obstacle to his Arab-led party joining a coalition headed by Gadi Eisenkot, according to The Times of Israel, citing a Hebrew media report. The Times of Israel reported that Abbas is scheduled to make the statement in an interview with journalist Dana Weiss on Channel 12. Confirming the broadcast, Abbas said in a statement carried by Channel 12, “On Saturday night, my interview with [journalist] Dana Weiss will be broadcast on Channel 12 news. I will address the definition of Hamas.” Abbas added that media coverage should address only “my words in the interview, and not other words attributed to me.” A public designation of Hamas as a terror group would mark a major departure for Abbas, who previously served in Israel’s governing coalition from 2021 to 2022 and ran Jewish candidate Yoav Segalovitz alongside Ra’am ahead of last month’s election to broaden its appeal and signal readiness for a coalition role. Previously, Abbas condemned acts of terror, including Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, but refrained from labelling Hamas a terror group, arguing that doing so allowed him to serve as a “bridge” and helped protect his family. The Joint List, the other Arab-led party, has likewise not publicly recognised Hamas as a terror group, according to Times of Israel. Eisenkot, who has nine days left on his mandate to form a government, has required every party in his coalition to recognise Hamas as a terror group and pledge its destruction. Meeting that condition could open a path for Ra’am into an Eisenkot-led government and help assemble a majority to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In a teaser for the Saturday evening Channel 12 interview, Weiss asks Abbas to confirm the meaning of a blurred text on a laptop screen before asking, “Have you reconciled yourself to the possibility that this step you’re taking could cost you your life?” Abbas, as quoted by the Times of Israel, replied: “I’ve reconciled myself to it.” According to The Times of Israel, citing a report by Ynet, Ra’am’s entry into an Eisenkot government remains contingent on policy demands, chiefly curbing crime in Arab municipalities, even if the Hamas declaration is made. Earlier, Abbas claimed that his party and the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) would join a proposed government led by Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, with the Joint List providing parliamentary support from outside the coalition. Speaking in an interview with Radio Makan on Thursday, Abbas said the political bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu was nearing an agreement to establish a new government, The Jerusalem Post reported. Abbas outlined a possible coalition arrangement involving the four parties belonging to the change bloc, alongside UTJ and his United Arab List (Ra’am), with the Joint List extending external parliamentary support. Eisenkot's Yashar party has reportedly indicated that it aims to form a government as early as next week without requesting an extension of its mandate from President Isaac Herzog. While the approval from the Lithuanian ultra-Orthodox leadership could pave the way for formal coalition negotiations, a final decision on joining the prospective government remains pending. (ANI)

item.title: Oscar-winning producer Gerald R Molen passes away at 91
item.description: Gerald R Molen, the Oscar-winning Hollywood producer known for his association with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and films such as ‘Schindler’s List’, ‘Jurassic Park’ and ‘Minority Report’, has died at ...
item.content:encoded:
Oscar-winning producer Gerald R Molen passes away at 91 Gerald R Molen, the Oscar-winning Hollywood producer known for his association with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and films such as ‘Schindler’s List’, ‘Jurassic Park’ and ‘Minority Report’, has died at the age of 91, according to The Hollywood Reporter. ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 10:10 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 10:10 IST

Late producer Gerald R Molen with director Steven Spielberg and Branko Lustig (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Gerald R Molen, the Oscar-winning Hollywood producer known for his association with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and films such as ‘Schindler’s List’, ‘Jurassic Park’ and ‘Minority Report’, has died at the age of 91, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Molen, a longtime resident of Bigfork, Montana, died on Monday, his great-niece Rachel Lorraine Pullan announced. The veteran producer shared the Best Picture Academy Award for Spielberg's ‘Schindler’s List’ (1993) with the filmmaker and Branko Lustig. Molen first collaborated with Spielberg as a unit production manager on ‘The Color Purple’ (1985). The filmmaker subsequently offered him his first producing assignment as an associate producer on “Batteries Not Included” (1987), according to The Hollywood Reporter. After working as a producer on Spielberg's ‘Hook’ (1991), Molen was appointed head of production at Amblin Entertainment, where he oversaw several projects, including ‘The Flintstones’ (1994), ‘The Little Rascals’ (1994), ‘Little Giants’ (1994), ‘Casper’ (1995), 'Twister' (1996) and ‘The Lost World: Jurassic Park’ (1997). Recalling his experience working at Amblin Entertainment in a 2023 interview, Molen said, “It was the best job in Hollywood, because any movie Spielberg directed I got to produce, and any movie the company did I got to oversee,” according to The Hollywood Reporter. Apart from his association with Spielberg and Amblin, Molen also produced several notable films, including the Best Picture Oscar winner ‘Rain Man’ (1988), ‘Days of Thunder’ (1990), ‘The Other Side of Heaven’ (2001), ‘Just Like Heaven’ (2005), ‘The Meg’ (2018) and ‘Meg 2: The Trench’ (2023). Born Gerald Robert Molen on January 6, 1935, in Great Falls, Montana, he moved with his family to North Hollywood in 1947. His parents, Gerald Sr. and Edith, later established a cafe across the street from Republic Pictures in Studio City. Speaking about his early fascination with filmmaking in a 2014 interview, Molen recalled how studio guards would allow him onto the film sets. “I got to make friends with the studio guards,” he said. “They used to take me on the studio lot and take me to a soundstage or the backlot where they were maybe shooting a Western and stuff me down behind a bale of hay or under a wagon. I got it in my blood.” After completing high school, Molen enlisted in the United States Marine Corps. Following 10 months of service, he joined Republic Pictures in 1957 as a truck driver, transporting furniture, according to The Hollywood Reporter. He moved to Universal Studios in 1959 and also had an early on-screen association with Alfred Hitchcock's ‘Psycho’ (1960). Molen doubled for actor Anthony Perkins in a scene featuring a car travelling towards the Bates Motel, with Hitchcock himself seated in the back seat giving directions. Molen subsequently rose to become head of transportation at Universal. Working as a transportation coordinator, captain and supervisor, he was associated with films such as ‘Escape to Witch Mountain’ (1975), ‘Bound for Glory’ (1976), ‘Coming Home’(1978), ‘Being There’ (1979), ‘Ordinary People’ (1980) and ‘Absence of Malice’ (1981). He later transitioned into unit production management, working on ‘The Postman Always Rings Twice’ (1981), ‘Tootsie’ (1982), ‘A Soldier’s Story’ (1984) and Spielberg's ‘The Color Purple’, before establishing himself as a film producer. Molen also made cameo appearances in several films, including ‘Rain Man’, ‘Days of Thunder’, ‘Jurassic Park’, ‘Amistad’ (1997) and ‘Catch Me If You Can’ (2002), the latter two directed by Spielberg. In addition to mainstream Hollywood productions, Molen produced the political documentaries ‘2016: Obama’s America’ (2012) and ‘Hillary’s America: The Secret History of the Democratic Party’(2016). Both films were written and directed by Dinesh D’Souza and were critical of Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton. With a career spanning several decades, Molen remained associated with some of Hollywood's notable productions, particularly through his long-running professional collaboration with Spielberg, according to The Hollywood Reporter. (ANI)
